move: satellites blob out of a core and back through goo filter
how: An SVG group filtered by feGaussianBlur (18) plus an alpha-contrast feColorMatrix, the classic goo filter, holds a central circle, six satellites and a drop. A seek function moves each satellite out to 200-280px along its own angle and back on a sine over D with phase i/6, spinning around the core and swelling radius up to 1.2x when fully out, so blobs stretch, neck and snap free of the core then rejoin. The core wobbles scaleX/scaleY plus or minus 0.12 three times per D, a drop falls from the top twice per D and dissolves into the core, and the group fill hue drifts plus or minus 40deg. Everything is periodic so the 8s loop closes.
adapt: Change the fill colour and background, satellite count and radii, and the caption word; the goo filter values (blur 18, alpha 28/-12) set how sticky the merge looks. Keep the phase-offset orbits so blobs leave one at a time.
port: mount(el, shot) injects the SVG with a uniquely-id filter and circles; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate sets cx, cy, r and the fill, replacing fx.register. gsap.min.js is loaded but unused in the original.
caveats: loads gsap but does not use it
full-group feGaussianBlur filter is slow at large sizes
